subject: Human Evolution
title: Lucy's Discovery
description: A short lesson to help you apply Lucy's Discovery.

hook.text: In 1974, Donald Johanson found a tiny arm bone sticking out of an Ethiopian hillside. Then more appeared.

buildup.text: Over weeks, 40% of a skeleton emerged—an extraordinary amount for a fossil 3.2 million years old.

discovery.text: Named Lucy (after the Beatles song), she was Australopithecus afarensis—small-brained but fully bipedal.

twist.text: Lucy was only 1.1 meters tall and weighed 29 kg, yet she walked upright like us across open ground.

climax.text: She proved upright walking evolved millions of years before large brains—flipping the old assumption.

punchline.text: A metre-tall woman redrew the human family tree.
